# Issue 7033 triage notes

## Assessment

**Does not reproduce; fixed in stable release v1.9.2602.** The complete, as-filed
single-file repro now compiles successfully. Closing as fixed is appropriate.

## Current ground truth

- `manual-case-main-debug-version.txt` records the required pre-probe version check. The
  Debug binary self-reports fork-local merge `7665270b9`; its compiler source is equivalent
  to public upstream commit `89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df`.
- `out-main-debug.txt` records the exact filed options and exit 0. The generated SPIR-V
  contains `DebugTypeComposite`, `DebugTypeTemplate`, and `DebugLocalVariable` records for
  the ray-query variable.
- `variant-no-rayquery-main-debug.txt` is the declared negative control. The same rich-debug
  configuration without `RayQuery` exits 0 and does not trip the internal-failure predicate.
- `match.json` uses `internal_failure`, covering the access-violation and SIGSEGV forms of
  this crash rather than depending on one message.

## Stable-release history

`bisect` found:

- v1.6.2112 reproduces with access violation `0xC0000005`;
- v1.8.2505.1 is the last reproducing stable release;
- v1.9.2602 is the first non-reproducing stable release and emits the expected rich debug
  records; v1.9.2607 is also clean.

The four older stable releases through v1.6.2106 are invalid probes because they reject
`-HV 2021` before parsing the shader. Five usable prereleases were excluded by stable-release
policy. `manual-case-history-controls.txt`, generated by `measure-history-controls.py`,
checks both sides of the instrument on every release probed by the bisection: the ray query
without rich debug and rich debug without a ray query. Both controls compile on every
probeable release from v1.6.2112 onward, while both fail with the same unsupported HLSL mode
on the four releases classified invalid.

## Fix evidence and thread history

The reporter supplied both the complete Compiler Explorer repro and
`attachment-debug_rayquery.patch`. Timeline evidence is in `timeline.json` and
`manual-case-cross-references.txt`; linked issue 7300 independently records the same
access violation in v1.8.2502.

PR 7139 merged as `61de7411f952cb0c4b6c73091555dad6419180ee` on 2025-11-05. The merge adds
`TK_RayQueryKHR` handling to `DebugTypeVisitor::lowerToDebugType` and adds a regression test.
`manual-case-fix-provenance.txt`, generated by `measure-fix-provenance.ps1`, records the diff
and proves that this merge is an ancestor of v1.9.2602 and the tested upstream-equivalent
commit, but not v1.8.2505.1. Ancestry proves the change is present in the fixing release, not
that it is the fix, so the attribution was then measured directly.

`manual-case-fix-commit.txt`, generated by `measure-fix-commit.py`, records Release `dxc`
built from detached worktrees at `61de7411f` and at its first parent
`b0245e32fdcf412850ed073476669f3a83fa5a76`. The two worktrees pin identical submodules, so the
only source difference is that commit's own diff. The as-filed command fails on the parent with
exit `0xE0000001` (`Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert`) and exits 0 on the commit, while
`control-no-rayquery.hlsl` compiles cleanly on both. The parent still failing and the commit
not failing is what identifies `61de7411f` as the exact fixing commit; the binaries self-report
`1.8.0.5092 (b0245e32f)` and `1.8.0.5093 (61de7411f)`.

The parent's internal failure presents here as an assert (`0xE0000001`) where the shipped
release binaries present the same defect as an access violation (`0xC0000005`). Both satisfy
`internal_failure`, which is the reason that predicate keys on internal-failure status rather
than on message text.

The verified Compiler Explorer link is https://godbolt.org/z/EbMbKx9d9.
`manual-case-godbolt-verify.txt` records dxc 1.6.2112 exiting 139 (`SIGSEGV`) and current
trunk exiting 0 with rich debug records.
